core.title: Keep plan artifacts at their canonical paths under the plan root
core.given: A declaration of a plan artifact (any kind the stack treats as a plan artifact) exists or is being written anywhere in the repository outside the vendored and generated trees this check excludes, with any filename suffix
core.when: its location is checked or the document is written
core.then: Every such declaration must sit at the canonical path for its kind under the configured plan root.
prefer: On a finding, move the document to the canonical path the finding names.
Resolve the plan root from the repository's root configuration rather than hard-coding a directory.
avoid: Keeping a second plan layout alongside the canonical one in the same repository.
Placing plan documents at ad-hoc paths and relying on identity lookup alone to find them.
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned.
core.why: The plan is navigated by path as much as by identity. A document at a non-canonical path is found by nothing that walks the layout, and two layouts in one repository make every tool guess.
evidence: The stack's plan-location check reports no finding for any plan declaration.
Every plan declaration resolves to the canonical path for its kind under the configured plan root.
verification: Strict disposition, severity 3: every finding fails; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

The check discovers plan declarations by content — a classifier recognising a document as a plan declaration whatever its path or filename suffix, including existing documents that were never moved — across the whole repository except the vendored and generated trees it itself excludes; a declaration with a noncanonical suffix or at a noncanonical path is a finding.
The check applies to every declaration, existing or new, wherever found; discovery is not narrowed by a path or suffix filter.
Findings must name the canonical target path; the fix is to move the document to the path the finding names.

The check does not scan vendored and generated trees; this check itself owns the exact exclusion list for them, kept in the realization. It neither restates that list as, nor inherits additional trees from, the stack-wide exclusion union.
The check does not cover production source or test files; the stack's source-location and test-location rules cover those roots.

values: plan-location finding naming the canonical target path

fires: An existing plan declaration sits somewhere other than the canonical path for its kind.
A plan declaration is stored under a noncanonical filename suffix.
A new or relocated plan declaration is written somewhere other than the canonical path for its kind.
A declaration sits outside the plan root, outside its owning unit's directory under it, or nested deeper than its canonical path.
A plan item document is at a path other than the canonical pattern for its kind.
The plan-location check reports a finding.
doesNotFire: Plan-shaped documents inside the vendored and generated trees this check excludes.
A plan declaration already at its canonical path with the canonical suffix.
Files whose content is not a plan declaration, whatever their path or suffix.
Production source and test files, which the stack's source-location and test-location rules cover.

profileRequirements.meaning: The root under which every plan declaration must live; the canonical paths are expressed relative to it and it is resolved from configuration, never hard-coded.
The repository file that declares the plan root, so the rule can resolve the plan root from configuration.

Discovery scope of the repository-wide location check: the whole repository, every file whatever its suffix. (The exact vendored/generated trees skipped by this check are owned by the check's realization, not by this key.)
profileRequirements.bunValue: `**/*` — the whole repository, every file whatever its suffix

profileRequirements.meaning: The plan-artifact kinds whose declarations the rule locates, recognised by content.
The canonical suffix a plan declaration's path must carry; any other suffix is noncanonical and is a finding.

The canonical path of a plan declaration under the plan root. The pattern is kind-dependent: one alternative per plan-artifact kind of roles.plan_artifact.kinds, each embedding the canonical suffix; a declaration of that kind at any other path is a finding.

The positive glob (whole repository, every file whatever its suffix) is the scan scope; the four negated globs are this checker's own exclusion list, preserved in bunOnly (unless[0], verifier_detail[2]) rather than in a profile key. There is no neutral activation-fact type for scan scope, so the core's given and the content-based-discovery verification entry carry it.
Neutral fact: file_kind 'plan_artifact', needs a content classifier regardless of path or suffix, including never-moved documents; 'wagon, feature, wmbt' are the profile kind names.
The finding id and validator name are realization details (bunOnly); generically, the location check emits findings naming the canonical path, which is the core's neutral finding fact.

neutralityNotes: No keys are proposed: the per-kind canonical paths are expressed as kind-dependent alternatives of the existing layout.plan_item, relative to roots.plan. The exact vendored/generated exclusion list is owned by this check's realization (the four trees are kept in bunOnly); the core keeps the neutral exception plus an ownership statement in verification and deliberately references neither the stack-wide roots.excluded union (which is broader and would change this rule's discovery scope) nor a rule-specific redefinition of it. The Bun kind names (wagon, feature, WMBT) survive only as profile values (roles.plan_artifact.kinds, layout.plan_item), never in the core text. The discovery-scope glob activation fact has no neutral activation-fact type (role|operation|change|phase|finding|file_kind|task_term|task_has_acceptance); its content is carried by the core's given, the content-based-discovery verification entry, and roots.scan. Per-rule severity (3) and strict disposition stay in core verification, and the finding/validator ids stay bunOnly, per the notProfileKeys list.
